name: Hematite
description: Heavy, cool and mirror-bright. Hematite is traditionally worn to feel anchored and to draw scattered focus back into the body.
mineral: Hematite is an iron oxide and the main ore of iron. Polished, it turns a mirror-bright silver-grey, and it feels noticeably heavier than other beads of the same size.
wornFor: A hematite bracelet is traditionally worn for grounding, focus and steadiness when a day feels scattered. Hematite belongs to the root chakra and is linked with Aries and Aquarius. Its weight is part of the appeal: many people notice it on the wrist, which makes it a physical reminder to slow down. Keep it dry, because iron can rust and lose its mirror shine.
wristWhy: Wear hematite on the right wrist. Grounding and protection pieces traditionally sit on the projecting side, and hematite is the steadying stone in The Guardian and The Anchor.
waterNote: Hematite is iron oxide and can rust, so wipe it with a dry cloth instead of rinsing it.
